Impulse	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
Cubic	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys	cubic a=.50, approximates sync (*)
Simon	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell    mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen	approximating B-spline (+)
Notch	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4	 good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6	 good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
Sinc4	 good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
Nearest	 fastest and crudest, sample the nearest texel from the appropriate mipmap level (%)
Bilinear	 remove blockiness, sample and interpolate the four nearest texels from the appropriate mipmap level (%)
Trilinear	 smooth interpolation of texture quality according to the distance, bilinearly interpolate between two closest mipmap levels (%)
Anisotropic	 highest quality filtering, gives a better result when shading surfaces with a high angle relative to the camera (%)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement
(%) constant time filter independent from the requested sampling area.It generates at rendering time mip map levels and could haveperformance impact when the texture is changing over time.

Randomly orbit camera about a point at the focus distance in front of it for each sample to produce depth-of-field effects from multiple samples.
Focus distance is set in the Camera, in the Projection tab.
Limit recursive subdivision by a screen-space distance percentage.

Select the motion vector render:
  • off - do not render the motion vector
  • classic - classic way to compute the motion vector
  • velocity - stores velocity in the motion vector channel
  • distance - stores distance between samples in the motion vector channel
In many cases, the classic (pre-Nuke 6.1) way to compute motion vectors was not accurate enough. The classic option is present so that existing scripts will still render as expected when they were created. Use the others options to have better results. In particular the distance mode in combination with the VectorBlur Node allows you to generate curved motion blur in a rendering with multiple samples per pixel.
output vectors
The number of pixels to render beyond the left/right and top/bottom of frame, if requested by subsequent operations.

The projection modes are:
Perspective: Objects in front of the camera have the illusion of depth defined by the camera's focal-length and aperture.
Orthographic: Objects are viewed using a parallel projection.
UV: Every object renders its UV space into the output format. Use this to cook out texture maps.
SphericalMap: The entire 360deg world is rendered as a spherical map. Lower the tessellation threshold knob to increase the accuracy of object edges as they are warped out of line (takes longer to render of course).
Render Camera: Take the projection mode from the camera.
Number of samples to render per pixel, to produce motion blur and antialiasing. If you use this, you can probably turn off the antialiasing and filter controls on the first tab.
This is how long the shutter should be open for when motion blurring. The value is in frames, so 0.5 is half a frame.

If the shutteroffset parameter is set to 'custom', this parameter is used to set the time that the shutter opens by adding it to the current frame.

Values are in frames, so -0.5 would open the shutter half a frame before the current frame.

The value of this controls how the shutter behaves with respect to the current frame value. It has four options
  • centred - centres the shutter around the frame, ie: open from f - shutter/2 to f + shutter/2
  • start - opens the shutter starting at the frame, ie: open from f to f + shutter
  • end - closes the shutter at the frame, ie: open from f - shutter to f
  • custom - opens the shutter at the time specified by the shuttercustomoffset parameter.
Diameter of circle that the samples for each pixel are placed in, for antialiasing.

Number of samples per pixel to use in stochastic estimation. Zero disables stochastic sampling. It is recommended for motion blur that the number of scenes to sample (samples knob) is adjusted. This will also provide anti-aliasing by jittering the sample point.
Add randomness to the distribution of the samples in time so they don't produce regularly spaced images.
Use a uniform temporal distribution of scenes to samples.This generates more accurate results for stochastic multisampling.
Type of ramp to use to blend two surfaces within the Z-blend range of each other. Smooth looks better, but linear is provided for back-compatibility.
Two surfaces closer than this distance from each other in Z are blended together, to smooth the transition between intersecting objects.

description.text:
Scanline Render

'obj/scn' input: (required) Scene containing objects or an individual object to be rendered.

When connected to a Scene all the objects and lights connected to that scene will be rendered.

'cam' input: (optional) Viewing camera. If the camera input is not connected, the renderer will use a default camera positioned at the origin and facing in the negative Z direction.

'bg' input: (optional) Determines the output format and background. If not used, will default to root.format or root.proxy_format.

Deep Data Output
Scanline Render has the ability to output Deep data. It will only produce this data if there is a Deep node downstream.
